events.title: Gustav Vasa Becomes King of Sweden
events.description: Gustav Vasa was elected King of Sweden, which ended the Kalmar Union. That union had bound Sweden, Denmark and Norway under one crown for more than a century.
events.significance: Sweden regained its independence, and Gustav Vasa founded a dynasty that shaped the country's development as a modern nation.

events.title: Alexander Pushkin Is Born
events.description: Alexander Pushkin was born in Moscow on this date by the modern Gregorian calendar. He became one of Russia's greatest poets and writers.
events.significance: Pushkin is widely regarded as the founder of modern Russian literature. His work shaped the Russian literary language.

events.title: The First Drive-In Movie Theater Opens
events.description: The first drive-in theater opened in Camden, New Jersey. It let audiences watch films from their cars.
events.significance: The drive-in became a symbol of American car culture and a popular form of entertainment in the mid-20th century.

events.title: D-Day: Allied Forces Land in Normandy
events.description: Allied troops landed on the beaches of Normandy, France, in Operation Overlord, under the overall command of General Dwight D. Eisenhower. It was the largest seaborne invasion in history.
events.significance: The landings opened a major Western front against Nazi Germany and were a turning point in the liberation of Western Europe.
